title: Why agents should never see your API keys
description: Pasting sk_live_ into Cursor works — until you have to rotate. Here's the safer pattern: vault once, inject on the tool call.
author: MCKey
html:
Builders moving fast paste Stripe and GitHub keys into AI chats because it's the lowest-friction way to ship an integration. The agent helps. Then it says rotate that key — because the secret is now in model context, chat logs, and whoever retains prompts.

The habit loop

Paste → ship → rotate → update .env → paste again next sprint. Security theater with real blast radius.

The MCKey pattern

  1. Seal the secret once in a local or hosted vault.
  2. Give the agent a handle (mckey://stripe) or an allowlisted MCKey.
  3. On MCP tool calls, inject the real credential outside the model.

Chat intercept is optional and better than sharing with the AI — not a guarantee. Prefer the vault path.

Try it

Install the local MCP gateway, seal a test key, and call http_request with {{SECRET:STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}}. The model never needs the value.
